_note: The device-platform whitelist: which hardware platforms may enrol a key under a trace-admitted substrate, and HOW each proves it is a genuine, un-tampered instance rather than a laptop asserting a string. The device-side analogue of the sources registry. Platforms are grouped into FAMILIES: NVIDIA Orin is one member of the edge-AI family the way Sentinel-2 is one source of the Earth substrate, and the population grows family by family toward the full device world the protocol means to integrate. Grounding: IETF RATS (RFC 9334) roles (Attester -> Evidence -> Verifier appraises vs Endorsements + Reference Values -> Relying Party); EAT (RFC 9711) evidence tokens; TCG DICE and IEEE 802.1AR DevID for layered/birth identity; TPM 2.0 measured boot; Intel TDX / AMD SEV-SNP / Arm confidential compute; Apple Secure Enclave and Android Keystore for mobile. A trust_anchor is an Endorsement (a vendor key vouching for a platform CLASS); reference_values (roadmap) endorse a specific DEVICE. HONESTY: every platform is status=candidate and every anchor is provisional=true. We hold no published vendor anchors and device ingest is not open; the shapes are pinned so device makers and the enrolment gate can build against them. A provisional anchor whitelists nothing until replaced with a published anchor.

families.title: Edge AI compute modules
families.description: On-device AI compute for robots, drones, and smart cameras: a Linux SoC under a measured boot with a hardware root of trust, running perception and control alongside a sensor payload.

families.title: Trusted hosts and gateways
families.description: Servers, ground-segment ingest hosts, and industrial gateways whose boot is measured by a discrete TPM or a confidential-computing root of trust.

families.title: Secure microcontrollers and RTOS payloads
families.description: Small RTOS devices and secure elements: satellite payload computers, instrument controllers, and fixed sensors that produce a PSA/EAT initial attestation rather than a Linux measured boot.

families.title: Open silicon roots of trust
families.description: Silicon-level DICE roots of trust whose reference values are auditable rather than vendor-proprietary, the strongest end of the registry.

families.title: Automotive compute
families.description: In-vehicle autonomy and ADAS compute. A self-driving vehicle contributes as a mobile robot until a dedicated vehicle substrate profile ships.

families.title: Mobile secure elements
families.description: Phone and wearable secure elements that attest a hardware-backed key: Apple Secure Enclave, Android StrongBox / hardware Keystore.

platforms.title: NVIDIA Jetson Orin (AGX / NX / Nano) edge AI module

trust_anchors._note: Placeholder for NVIDIA's device-attestation CA. Orin derives a DICE layered identity; the alias/DeviceID cert chains here. Replace with the published SPKI fingerprint before going active.

platforms._note: The platform most operators mean by 'my robot/drone can write to emem'. Linux under a measured boot with a DICE root of trust, so the device_key is a DICE alias key whose certificate attests the hardware and boot layers.

platforms.title: NVIDIA Jetson Thor (next-gen robotics module)

trust_anchors._note: Same NVIDIA attestation domain as Orin; distinct reference values.

platforms._note: The successor robotics module. Same DICE-X509 path as Orin, higher on-device inference capacity, so the inference trace layer carries more weight.

platforms.title: Qualcomm Robotics RB5 / RB6 platform

trust_anchors._note: Qualcomm attests via Secure Boot + QTEE with Android hardware key attestation, an X.509 chain to a Qualcomm/Google root. Pin that root here.

platforms._note: Robotics on Qualcomm silicon. Attestation is an X.509 key-attestation chain rather than a DICE/EAT token; lower structural assurance than measured-boot DICE until firmware measurements are pinned as reference values.

platforms.title: Rockchip RK3588 edge SoC

trust_anchors._note: Arm TrustZone / OP-TEE secure world signer. A PSA-style attestation is only as strong as the firmware provisioning; treat as candidate until measurements are published.

platforms._note: A common low-cost edge SoC for cameras and light robotics. TrustZone-based PSA attestation; included so the registry is not NVIDIA-only.

platforms.title: Linux host with a discrete TPM 2.0 (measured boot + PCR quote)

trust_anchors._note: Per-deployment: the operator pins the EK/AK CA of the TPM vendor(s) it runs. There is no single global TPM anchor.

platforms._note: The ground-segment ingest host and industrial gateway. Evidence is a TPM 2.0 quote over the boot PCRs signed by an attestation key whose cert chains to the TPM vendor EK CA. The first-step path a satellite operator uses before the flight computer itself attests.

platforms.title: Intel TDX confidential VM

trust_anchors._note: Intel DCAP PCK certificate root. A TD quote is appraised against this chain plus the TDX module reference values.

platforms._note: A confidential VM for ingest or processing that must prove the exact software stack ran unmodified. The measured launch of the TD is the evidence; useful where the operator will not run bare metal.

platforms.title: AMD SEV-SNP confidential VM

trust_anchors._note: AMD ARK/ASK root. A SEV-SNP attestation report is signed by the VCEK, whose certificate chains here.

platforms._note: The AMD counterpart to Intel TDX in the confidential-host family. Report is VCEK-signed; measurement of the guest launch digest is what a reader appraises.

platforms.title: Arm PSA Certified L2 device (RTOS / MCU class)

trust_anchors._note: Signer of the PSA initial attestation token for the device's secure firmware. PSA attestation IS an EAT profile.

platforms._note: The flight/payload computer and instrument controller. Small RTOS devices (Zephyr, Trusted Firmware-M) producing a PSA/EAT token rather than a Linux measured boot.

platforms.title: Arm PSA Certified L3 device (SESIP L3 / tamper-resistant)

trust_anchors._note: PSA L3 adds physical tamper resistance to the L2 attestation. Same EAT path, higher assurance level.

platforms._note: The high-assurance secure element: L3 defends against physical attack, the level to require where a sensor sits in an adversarial location.

platforms.title: RISC-V Keystone enclave

trust_anchors._note: Keystone security-monitor measurement root. Open TEE on open ISA, so the reference values can be published and audited.

platforms._note: An open-source enclave on an open ISA. Included alongside the proprietary secure MCUs so a builder wanting an auditable stack has a path.

platforms.title: Caliptra (OCP) DICE root of trust

trust_anchors._note: Caliptra is an open silicon-level DICE RoT; the anchor is the integrator's provisioning CA. Reference values are auditable.

platforms._note: The datacenter/industrial end: an open silicon DICE root of trust whose measured firmware can be checked against published known-good values, not just a vendor signature.

platforms.title: OpenTitan silicon root of trust

trust_anchors._note: OpenTitan provisioning CA. Open silicon RoT with a DICE-CBOR certificate chain; auditable like Caliptra.

platforms._note: An open, transparent silicon root of trust for discrete secure elements. Pairs with Caliptra as the auditable-silicon path.

platforms.title: NVIDIA DRIVE Orin (automotive)

trust_anchors._note: NVIDIA DRIVE attestation domain, distinct from the Jetson robotics line; automotive safety firmware.

platforms._note: In-vehicle autonomy compute. A self-driving vehicle contributes as a mobile robot until a dedicated vehicle substrate profile ships; recorded here so automotive is a first-class family.

platforms.title: Qualcomm Snapdragon Ride (automotive)

trust_anchors._note: Qualcomm automotive attestation root (X.509 key attestation).

platforms._note: The Qualcomm counterpart in the automotive family. X.509 key attestation as on RB5, in a functional-safety envelope.

platforms.title: Apple Secure Enclave (iOS / macOS)

trust_anchors._note: Apple's app-attest / DeviceCheck attestation root. Keys are Secure-Enclave-bound; the attestation vouches for a genuine, unmodified device.

platforms._note: A phone or wearable as a handheld sensor. The Secure Enclave attests a hardware-bound key; the OS-signpost trace is the execution evidence. Grain and tempo come from the mobile substrate profile.

platforms.title: Android StrongBox / hardware Keystore

trust_anchors._note: Google hardware attestation root. A StrongBox key attestation is an X.509 chain to this root that also encodes the verified-boot state.

platforms._note: The Android counterpart in the mobile family. StrongBox is a dedicated secure element; the key attestation carries the verified-boot state a reader can appraise.
